We've seen many reports about Apple Vision Pro applications in medical settings. This week, Stryker announced the completion of the first surgical procedure performed using an innovative Vision Pro application.

The procedure was a hip arthroscopy using the SportSuite Vision application, which can bring "critical digital content into the virtual space of the operating room." This includes arthroscopic imagery, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images.

Here's Stryker's description of the application:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's visual field, allowing them to simultaneously view physical objects and digital tools in the operating room, such as arthroscopic imagery, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images. During arthroscopic procedures, surgeons often rely on multiple displays placed throughout the operating room to access imagery and surgical data. By consolidating multiple data sources into the surgeon's field of view, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional displays and support a smoother, more ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorization on July 17. Stryker states this is the first FDA-approved application for use with Vision Pro during surgical procedures.
